# Textarea

> A minimalist text editor that runs entirely in your browser. Notes live in the
> URL, in a document library in your own browser, or — if you ask for it — in a
> folder you pick on your own disk; nothing is uploaded, there is no account,
> and there is no server.

This is a fork of [antonmedv/textarea](https://github.com/antonmedv/textarea).
The site is static — `index.html`, `app.js` (the entry) and the modules under `lib/` — so
there is no API to call, no account to hold, and nothing here to authenticate
against. Everything below is the behaviour of that one page.

What usually needs answering:

- **Where is a note kept?** Compressed into the URL fragment (`#…`), which
  browsers never send to a server, and mirrored into IndexedDB about half a
  second after you stop typing. An opt-in **folder sync** mirrors the library
  both ways with a folder you pick, as one markdown file per note with a small
  front matter block; newest wins and deletions mirror. Export writes it out
  as a file, on the clipboard, as a QR code, or as a ZIP archive.
- **Does anything leave the machine?** No note ever does: no network call
  carries note content, the third-party libraries are cached locally by a
  service worker, and clearing site data deletes the library. The one
  outbound read is the font shelf's GitHub import — a link you paste, one
  file fetched from `raw.githubusercontent.com` and nowhere else, only while
  its button is pressed. Folder sync writes files to a folder on your own
  disk and nowhere else — plaintext markdown, because that is what makes
  them editable in any other program — and it never removes a file it did
  not write itself. The library is a local backup, not a network sync
  service: deleting a note parks it in a trash beside the library for 30
  days (one click brings it back), and **Backup** writes every note into a
  single ZIP in Folder sync's own file format — the copy to take before a
  browser profile goes away.
- **Is there an AI feature, and does it phone home?** Two, and neither
  does. **Speech to text** records from the microphone or takes an audio
  file and transcribes it with Whisper (small, or large v3 turbo on WebGPU) through a
  vendored transformers.js, on weights committed under `models/` in
  checksum-verified chunks; the audio never leaves the page. The writing tools are
  five one-press rewrites (improve, shorten, summarise, fix grammar, make
  casual) with a line of your own instructions appended, run by Gemma 3
  270M, MiniCPM5 2B or MiniCPM-V 4.7 1B (which also describes and reads
  images), all shipped with the repository in chunks under `models/`,
  each checked against a pinned SHA-256 before anything loads, fetched and
  cached by the site itself. The prompt is at most 24,000 characters of the
  note — or of just the selection, behind a second switch that ships off —
  and it never leaves the machine; the feature is off until its switch
  is thrown, and the engine and weights are fetched on the first run
  rather than at boot.
- **What is encrypted, and with what?** AES-256-GCM, both for an encrypted link
  (key derived from the password with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256) and for a WinZip AES
  archive. The password is never stored and never appears in the link, and a
  lost password cannot be recovered.
- **What can it open?** Text as UTF-8 with a Windows-1252 fallback, PDFs
  through pdf.js with two-column detection, and ZIP archives through zip.js —
  the last two fetched on demand, never from a CDN.
- **What can it write?** Nine formats: txt, md, html, json, csv, xml, rtf, tex
  and yaml, each on its own or in any combination inside one archive.
- **How do I find text, or tick a task?** Ctrl/Cmd+F opens the app's own
  find bar — match case, whole words, replace one or all — while its switch
  is on, which it is as it ships; off, the browser's find keeps the chord.
  A line starting `- [ ]` or `- [x]` draws as a clickable checkbox behind
  the Tasks switch (off as it ships), and a **Tasks** panel gathers every
  open task across the library with a jump to the note it came from. Every
  one of these is a switch in Settings.

- [Contributing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gitguy268/textarea/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): how the code is laid out, how to run the tests, and the two hard rules
